record.summary: Report of an expert working group that the Governor asked in September 2024 to help California develop guardrails for frontier AI. Without endorsing any bill, it sets out evidence-based policy principles in a 'trust but verify' approach: transparency on data acquisition, safety and security practices, pre-deployment testing and downstream impacts; independent verification of safety claims and risk assessments; whistleblower protections and safe harbours for third-party evaluators; adverse-event reporting to monitor post-deployment harms; and thresholds for intervention, based for example on compute or users, that can be revised over time.
record.notes: Draft released on 18 Mar 2025 for public feedback until 8 Apr 2025; final report 17 Jun 2025. Co-led by Jennifer Tour Chayes, Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar and Fei-Fei Li, with Rishi Bommasani and Scott R. Singer as lead writers; the co-leads write in their own capacity, not for their institutions. Requested in September 2024, the month of the Governor's veto of SB 1047 (US-CA-03), it focuses on frontier models and leaves out AI's effects on work, the environmental impact of data centres and the full range of misuse. SB 53 (2025) built on its recommendations.

verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the report PDF (gov.ca.gov, copy of 11 Oct 2026, unchanged on 17 Oct 2026), which gives the title, the working group, the date 17 Jun 2025, the co-leads and lead writers, the draft of 18 Mar 2025, the origin of the request in September 2024 and the eight key principles; and the Governor's release of 17 Jun 2025 (gov.ca.gov, copy of 17 Oct 2026), which says the group was convened at his request and released its final report that day. Also stored for this record: Executive Order N-9-26 (18 Sep 2026, gov.ca.gov PDF), whose recitals say the Governor convened the experts in 2024 and that SB 53 'built on the recommendations included in the report'. Version 1's claim that the independent-verification framework of SB 813 (2026) enacted the report's recommendations rests on no stored source and was removed.

The report does not argue for or against any particular piece of legislation or regulation.
this report derives policy principles that can inform how California approaches the use, assessment, and governance of frontier AI—principles rooted in an ethos of “trust but verify. ”

Carefully tailored policies can enhance transparency on key areas with current information deficits, such as data acquisition, safety and security practices, pre-deployment testing, and downstream impacts.
establishing robust mechanisms to independently verify safety claims and risk assess- ments
Clear whistleblower protections and safe harbors for third-party evaluators can enable increased transparency above and beyond information disclosed by foundation model developers.
Adverse event reporting systems enable monitoring of the post-deployment impacts of AI and commensurate modernization of existing regulatory or enforcement authorities.
Scoping which entities are covered by a policy often involves setting thresholds, such as com- putational costs measured in FLOP or downstream impact measured in users.
policymakers should ensure that mechanisms are in place to adapt thresholds over time

judgment.status_reasoning: A final, non-binding report published on 17 Jun 2025 (cover and citation; the Governor's release says the group 'today released its final report'). It argues for no legislation and offers principles that officials 'could consider'. Nothing stored shows a withdrawal or a newer edition, so 'Published (non-binding, current)' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: A report that the Governor requested from leading experts on frontier AI governance: a government-commissioned scientific report, in scope with no note (AGENTS.md section 10). The cover names the Joint California Policy Working Group on AI Frontier Models as author and the Governor's office published it; version 1's issuing body (the working group, convened by the Governor) is kept. If maintainers read the precedent on reports written by an expert group an authority convened as applying here, the issuing body would become the Governor of California with a scope_note naming the working group.
